target.title: fix(agents): add additionalProperties:false to Anthropic tool inputSchema for Opus 4.8 compat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tools.profile=coding` + `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` reliably fails with HTTP 400 because `projectAnthropicTools` omitted `additionalProperties: false` from the tool `input_schema` sent to Anthropic. Opus 4.8 enforces stricter tool schema validation than Opus 4.7.

- Problem: Anthropic tool projection omits `additionalProperties: false`, causing opus-4-8 to reject coding-profile tool schemas with HTTP 400 on every turn
- Solution: Add `additionalProperties: false` to the top-level `inputSchema` object in `projectAnthropicTools`, matching the strict closed-object normalization already used on OpenAI-family routes
- What changed: `src/agents/anthropic-tool-projection.ts` — type definition + runtime object (+2 lines)
- What did NOT change: Provider transport layer, OpenAI-family normalization, tool-projection behavior for other tool attributes, non-Anthropic paths

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98588
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Users pairing `tools.profile=coding` with `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` (the current Anthropic recommended coding-capable model) get HTTP 400 on every turn with no actionable guidance. The same profile works with opus-4-7 and the same model works with non-coding profiles. This is the Anthropic-side analogue of #60821, which was previously fixed for OpenAI/Copilot strict transports via `normalizeStrictOpenAIJsonSchema`.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `projectAnthropicTools` produced `input_schema` without `additionalProperties: false`, causing opus-4-8 to reject coding-profile tool schemas with HTTP 400
- Real environment tested: Linux x64, Node.js v22.19.0, branch `fix/anthropic-coding-tool-schema-98588`, upstream/main HEAD `be2c4c65ab`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { projectAnthropicTools } from './src/agents/anthropic-tool-projection.js'

const tools = [
  { name: "read", description: "Read a file from disk", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { path: { type: "string" } }, required: ["path"] } },
  { name: "write", description: "Write a file to disk", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { path: { type: "string" }, content: { type: "string" } }, required: ["path", "content"] } },
  { name: "execute", description: "Execute a shell command", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { command: { type: "string" }, cwd: { type: "string" } }, required: ["command"] } },
]

const projection = projectAnthropicTools(tools, (n) => n)
for (const t of projection.tools) {
  console.log(`${t.wireName}: additionalProperties=${JSON.stringify(t.inputSchema.additionalProperties)}`)
}
NODE
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { projectAnthropicTools } from './src/agents/anthropic-tool-projection.js'
const tools = [
  { name: "read", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { path: { type: "string" } }, required: ["path"] } },
  { name: "write", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { path: { type: "string" }, content: { type: "string" } }, required: ["path", "content"] } },
  { name: "execute", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { command: { type: "string" } }, required: ["command"] } },
]
const p = projectAnthropicTools(tools, n => n)
for (const t of p.tools) console.log(`${t.wireName}: additionalProperties=${JSON.stringify(t.inputSchema.additionalProperties)} type=${t.inputSchema.type}`)
NODE

read: additionalProperties=false type=object
write: additionalProperties=false type=object
execute: additionalProperties=false type=object
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. All projected tool `inputSchema` objects now include `additionalProperties: false` at the top level
  2. No changes to `type`, `properties`, `required`, or wire-name mapping
  3. Existing Anthropic transport-stream tests (82 tests) and provider tests (37 tests) continue to pass
  4. The schemas now satisfy strict closed-object validation, matching the OpenAI-family path's behavior after #60821
- What was not tested: Live Anthropic API call with opus-4-8 + coding profile (requires valid Anthropic API key targeting opus-4-8). ClawSweeper source-level review confirmed the fix direction is correct and the offending field is exactly the missing `additionalProperties: false`.

| Input schema after fix | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `additionalProperties` | absent (undefined) | `false` |
| `type` | `"object"` | `"object"` (unchanged) |
| `properties` | preserved | preserved (unchanged) |
| `required` | preserved | preserved (unchanged) |

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`projectAnthropicTools` in `src/agents/anthropic-tool-projection.ts` builds `inputSchema` with `type`, `properties`, and `required`, but had never included `additionalProperties: false`. This was tolerated by opus-4-7 but is now enforced by opus-4-8's stricter tool schema validation. The OpenAI-family transport path already applies equivalent strict closed-object normalization via `normalizeStrictOpenAIJsonSchema` (introduced in #60821), but the Anthropic transport path was missed.

Introduced by: the original `projectAnthropicTools` implementation (commit `6497c3ca1b7b`); made visible by opus-4-8's stricter schema enforcement.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Target: `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` (82 tests), `src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts` (37 tests)
- Coverage: Anthropic tool projection, payload construction, and provider conversion all exercise the changed code path
- Both test files pass ✅

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users pairing `tools.profile=coding` with `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` will no longer receive HTTP 400 "provider rejected the request schema or tool payload" errors. No other behavior change — existing opus-4-7 + coding profile combos are unaffected.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-level validation of `projectAnthropicTools` output with 3 coding-profile tools; all produce `additionalProperties: false`; existing test suites pass
- Edge cases checked: Empty properties array, missing required array, multiple tools in same projection
- What you did NOT verify: Live Anthropic API call with opus-4-8 (no valid API key targeting opus-4-8 available in this test environment)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — all existing tool schemas remain valid; `additionalProperties: false` is already the norm on OpenAI-family paths
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — adding `additionalProperties: false` at the shared projection layer (`projectAnthropicTools`) fixes both consumers (agent transport + provider path) in one place, following the same pattern as `normalizeStrictOpenAIJsonSchema` on OpenAI-family routes
- **Refactor needed**: No — this is a minimal, targeted fix
- **Alternative considered**: Running `normalizeStrictOpenAIJsonSchema` on the Anthropic tool payloads. Rejected because (a) that function does more than just add `additionalProperties: false` (it also normalizes `required` for empty `properties`), and (b) the scale of change is larger than this targeted fix. If Anthropic adds more strict-schema rules in the future, the two approaches can be unified then.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Risk**: The fix changes the serialized tool schema payload sent to Anthropic for all tools (not just coding-profile). A tool schema that was previously missing `additionalProperties: false` and relied on Anthropic's older permissive parsing could break.
**Mitigation**: `additionalProperties: false` is already the standard on OpenAI-family paths (via #60821) without reported regressions. Anthropic's own API docs recommend closed-object schemas. All existing test suites pass.
